access_denied: Access to the folder is denied, its contents were not checked
data_invalid: The built-in heuristics data is damaged, the heuristics work without it: {{error}}
dotfile: Settings file in the root of the user profile: usually the config of a developer tool
dotfolder: Hidden settings folder in the root of the user profile: usually created by a developer tool
uwp_saves: Saves of an Xbox / Microsoft Store game
uwp_package: Data of a Microsoft Store app
saved_games: The folder is in “Saved Games”: most likely these are game saves
unreal_saves: Looks like saves of an Unreal Engine game (SaveGames folder)
unity_game: Looks like data of a Unity game, it may contain saves
save_ext: Many files with game save extensions (.sav, .save, .sl2, .ess)
config_like: Small folder with program settings files
sqlite_recent: Recently changed SQLite databases: the program keeps its data here
user_content: Mostly documents, photos or other media files
unknown: Could not tell what this folder contains

junk.cache_name: Cache, temporary files or logs: no need to save them
junk.cache_like: Looks like a cache: the program creates these files again
junk.restorable: Dependencies or build output (node_modules, .venv, target and the like): they are restored from the project, no need to save them
junk.installed_program: Files of an installed program: it can be installed again after reinstalling Windows
junk.uniform_binaries: Looks like program files: executables with the same modification time, no settings or databases. The program can be installed again
junk.launcher: Launcher or game library folder: the games can be downloaded again through the launcher
junk.downloadable: Downloaded installers, updates or shader cache: all of it can be downloaded again

web.electron: Data of an Electron app: local storage, databases and settings. The cache is not saved
web.chromium: Chromium browser profile: bookmarks, settings and site data. The cache is not saved

dpapi_bound: Passwords and cookies are encrypted by Windows (DPAPI) for this user account: after reinstalling they cannot be decrypted, so you will have to sign in to all accounts again

usr.cluster: Folder with user files outside the standard locations (files: {{files}})
usr.valuable_file: Valuable file outside the folders with user files: a key, a certificate, a password database or a mail archive

usr_truncated: Too many folders with user files were found, only the most valuable ones are shown ({{limit}}). Folders not shown: {{count}}

git.no_remote: Git repository without a remote: its whole history exists only on this computer
git.unsaved: The git repository has unsaved work. Changed files: {{dirty}}, new files: {{untracked}}, unpushed commits: {{unpushed}}, stash entries: {{stash}}
git.unchecked: Could not fully check the git repository (some files are only in the cloud or a submodule was not read), so it is treated as having unsaved work. Found: changed files: {{dirty}}, new files: {{untracked}}, unpushed commits: {{unpushed}}, stash entries: {{stash}}
git.clean: All changes are committed and pushed to the server: the repository can be cloned again with git clone
git.failed: Could not read the state of the git repository: it may be damaged
git.not_analyzed: The git repository was not checked: more repositories were found than one scan checks
git.bundle: Alternative: save the whole history of the repository as one file (git bundle) together with the uncommitted files

git_failed: Could not read the git repository: {{error}}
git_truncated: Too many git repositories were found, only the first ones were checked ({{limit}}). Repositories not checked: {{count}}
